security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by SVG coordinates, Markdown text, regular-expression calls, or JavaScript template literals. Confirmed behavior includes official network requests, cache writes, environment reads, shell execution, and a curl fallback. Unrestricted sources and cache destinations create SSRF, argument-injection, local-read, and overwrite risks.

remediation.issue: The manual helper accepts arbitrary URLs and passes them to curl as options.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS on approved OpenAI hosts, reject cross-host redirects, and place an option terminator before the URL.

remediation.issue: The model resolver accepts arbitrary remote URLs and local file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Allow approved OpenAI hosts by default and require an explicit trusted-local-source flag for file access.

remediation.issue: The cache override can target any writable directory and replace fixed filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict cache paths to canonical temporary roots, reject unsafe directory links, and use a dedicated owned subdirectory.

semantic_findings.description: The manual URL accepts arbitrary targets and reaches curl without an option terminator, enabling internal requests or curl option injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI value is appended directly to curl arguments and no scheme, host, or option-prefix validation occurs.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Model Source Reads Local Files or Arbitrary URLs
semantic_findings.description: Environment variables and command arguments can select any local path or HTTP URL, bypassing the skill's official-domain boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The resolver explicitly accepts environment and CLI sources, then reads local files or fetches any HTTP endpoint.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Cache Directory Can Replace Files
semantic_findings.description: A user-selected cache directory receives fixed filenames through rename operations, which can replace existing files in any writable directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The override accepts any writable directory and atomically renames fixed cache filenames over existing entries.

content.user_title: Find Current OpenAI and Codex Documentation
content.value_statement: OpenAI products, models, and APIs change quickly, making remembered guidance unreliable. This skill retrieves current official documentation and provides concise, cited answers.
actual_capabilities: Searches and opens current official OpenAI documentation before answering.
Provides concise citations for API, model, product, and Codex claims.
Routes broad Codex setup questions through a verified manual and focused references.
Compares models using current documentation for quality, latency, cost, modality, and availability.
Guides model migrations, prompt updates, compatibility checks, and validation planning.
Diagnoses official documentation MCP setup when a user explicitly requests local configuration.
limitations: Search and citations are restricted to approved official OpenAI and ChatGPT domains.
Documentation cannot confirm account-specific access, rollout timing, quotas, or billing entitlements.
Bundled helpers require network access, Node.js 18 or newer, and a writable temporary directory.
Bundled fallback references may become outdated and must be disclosed when used.

use_cases.title: Verify API Behavior
use_cases.description: Confirm endpoints, request fields, SDK behavior, and error handling against current official documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Model Migration
use_cases.description: Compare targets and identify model, prompt, tool, state, compatibility, and testing changes.

use_cases.title: Configure Codex
use_cases.description: Find current guidance for Codex settings, skills, plugins, MCP, automations, setup, and troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Official Answer
prompt_templates.prompt: Find current official OpenAI documentation for [topic]. Answer [question] concisely and cite the supporting page.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused product or API question.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [model A] and [model B] for [workload] using current official documentation. Evaluate quality, latency, cost, modalities, and availability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when choosing between named models.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Verified Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration from [current model] to [target model] for [application]. Identify API, prompting, tool, state, compatibility, and testing changes with citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before changing a production model.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an OpenAI Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this OpenAI integration against current official documentation: [system description]. Identify unsupported assumptions, schema mismatches, migration risks, and the smallest verified fixes.

output_examples.input: Which OpenAI API should handle a stateful tool-using workflow?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use the documented Responses API workflow. The answer explains state handling, tool calls, limitations, and cites the relevant official guide.

output_examples.input: Plan our migration from a named model to a newer target.
output: Target decision based on current official model guidance.
Compatibility changes for requests, tools, reasoning, and state.
Prompt updates only where documented behavior requires them.
Validation checks and citations for each consequential change.

output_examples.input: Why is the OpenAI documentation MCP server unavailable in my local Codex client?
output_examples.output: A focused diagnostic covering supported setup, enabled state, policy, authorization, refresh requirements, and evidence needed before claiming success.

best_practices: Name the exact product, model, API, or Codex feature in the request.
Preserve explicitly requested models and state workload constraints before asking for recommendations.
Use cited official pages for current facts and disclose any bundled fallback.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for current pricing, availability, or limits without requiring official citations.
Do not treat a search snippet, memory, or bundled snapshot as current documentation.
Do not request configuration changes when only a documentation answer is needed.

faq.question: Which sources does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses official OpenAI developer documentation, platform documentation, ChatGPT Work learning pages, and narrowly selected bundled references.

faq.question: Can it choose an OpenAI model?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares documented workload fit, quality, latency, cost, modality, and availability while preserving any explicitly requested model.

faq.question: Can it update my application?
faq.answer: It can guide or implement requested changes after verifying current API and model documentation. API-backed execution may require a separate credential workflow.

faq.question: Does it know my account limits or access?
faq.answer: No. It states uncertainty when official documentation does not establish account-specific access, quotas, pricing, billing, or rollout status.

faq.question: What happens when live documentation is unavailable?
faq.answer: It may use a relevant bundled fallback, clearly disclose that choice, and warn that the information may be outdated.

faq.question: Can it configure the OpenAI documentation MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes, for a supported local Codex client after explicit authorization. It verifies current setup guidance and does not claim success without evidence.
